reflux_tier_why: Low (x0.7). Ice wins by laying cold over several casts and cashing it in once, so it must be able to cast four or five times in a row without locking; and cold is the opposite end of the heat axis from fire, which runs high. Its skills sit cheap to mid in essence.
rule: Cold stays: every ice hit adds Chill, which never wears off by itself; at 5 Chill the target freezes solid, and a frozen thing is Brittle, so the next hard hit Shatters it.
rule_refined_from: design/14 first pass: 'what it freezes stays frozen; cold builds up on a target until it locks solid; frozen things turn brittle and break'.
rule_why: The first pass is kept and made countable. 'Stays' becomes a concrete promise the player can see: Chill has no timer (only fire, Melt and Thaw take it off), where lightning's marks fade in 8 s. That is the line between the two build-up affinities: lightning's third mark goes off by itself and spreads; ice's fifth Chill only locks, and paying it out takes a deliberate hard hit. 'Hard hit' is defined with numbers the game already has (a bare strike, or 40+ poise), so base strikes and heavy skills from any affinity can Shatter. A frozen body takes half damage from everything but a Shatter, so freezing is control first and the payout must be chosen. Elites never lock; they go Brittle instead, so ice still has an answer to them.
_note: DRAFT 2026-10-22 [MODEL]. Ice is not in the game. One skill per base rune (runes.json ICE-1a..5b), three starters, an effect for each rune. Field names follow abilities.json; new keys are named in new_mechanics. 'blinded' (used by Whiteout and the Snow effect) is defined once, in dark.json (Pall). Kept apart from water (ice holds bodies still, it never moves them), earth (no blocking walls: Rime makes spikes, not slabs) and light.

skills.name: Set Solid
skills.summary: The air around you sets. Everything within 3.5 m takes 30 damage and 3 Chill: two more and it freezes solid.
skills.verb_fit: Freeze is 'lock solid'. Ice's lock is the fifth Chill, and this puts three on everything around you at once: anything already carrying two locks on the spot, and the rest are one Hoarline from it.

new_mechanics.name: chilled
new_mechanics.definition: Up to 5 stacks, no timer: each stack slows movement 8%. At 5 the target is Frozen and the stacks clear. Only fire (any Alight), Melt, Thaw, a Shatter, or 10 s with no enemy in sight takes Chill off.

new_mechanics.name: frozen
new_mechanics.definition: 1 stack, 3 s (heavy enemies 1.5 s): cannot move or act, takes half damage from everything except a Shatter, and counts as Brittle. If it runs out it leaves 2 Chill. Elites never freeze: at 5 Chill they are Brittle for 4 s instead.

new_mechanics.name: brittle
new_mechanics.definition: 1 stack, 5 s: the next hard hit on it (a bare strike, or any hit with 40+ poise damage) Shatters it.

new_mechanics.name: shatter
new_mechanics.definition: A hard hit on a Frozen or Brittle enemy: 100 damage to it, not halved, and shards hit every other enemy within 2.5 m for 40 and 1 Chill. Ends Frozen and Brittle. Talents see it as damage you dealt.

good_modifiers.word: The air sets farther out: 30% wider, a little less damage.
Sets at once: the 0.2 s wind-up drops by a quarter.
The ring grows spikes: harder, and more poise damage.
Sets them brittle as well: a bare strike Shatters what Set Solid only chilled.

bad_modifiers.why: Not a shot; nothing to pierce. Falls back.
The ring is a moment; the Chill it leaves already stays. No duration field; falls back.
The air sets where you stand; it does not travel. No speed field; falls back.

skills.name: False Spring
skills.summary: Every Frozen enemy within 10 m thaws at once, and the cold it held pours out: 50 damage and 3 Chill to every other enemy within 3 m of it. It frees what you froze, to freeze the ones beside it.
skills.verb_fit: Thaw is 'release, melt free'. This releases your own frozen enemies on purpose: they go free, and the cold that held them runs into their neighbours.

new_mechanics.name: thaw burst
new_mechanics.definition: detonate with consume_status 'frozen': each Frozen enemy in range is freed (it keeps the 2 Chill Frozen leaves) and on_hit is applied to every other enemy within burst_radius of it.

good_modifiers.word: The thaw spreads wider: 30% more room, a little less damage.
Reaches frozen bodies 14 m away.
What the thaw pours over is left Brittle: strike it.
A quicker spring: recovery a quarter shorter.

bad_modifiers.why: Freeze is Thaw's opposite, and the Chill it would add is already what the burst gives; a status op cannot add stacks to a status already applied. Falls back.
Not a shot. Falls back.
The thaw happens where the frozen bodies are; nothing travels. Falls back.

skills.name: Hoarline
skills.summary: A line of frost races 10 m along the ground: 45 damage and 2 Chill to everything on it. The line stays frosted for 4 s, adding a Chill a second to anyone standing on it. Walls stop it.
skills.verb_fit: Frost is 'creeping cold on the ground that grips and slows'. Hoarline is that cold, sent along the floor: it grips (Chill) and it slows (Chill again), and the ground keeps doing it after it has passed.

new_mechanics.name: projectile trail
new_mechanics.definition: A projectile may carry 'trail' (as Flashover's dash does): a strip of ground along its path that applies trail.payload every tick_s for trail.life.

new_mechanics.name: frosted ground
new_mechanics.definition: Ground left by an ice skill: 1 Chill a second to an enemy standing on it. Fire on it clears it.

good_modifiers.word: The frost runs 14 m, a little weaker.
The frosted line lingers 6 s.
Everything on the line is left Brittle: a strike Shatters the first one you reach.
A true, fast line: quicker and a little longer.

bad_modifiers.why: It already passes everything on the line. Falls back.
There is no wind-up to shorten; it leaves the hand at once. Falls back.

skills.name: Black Ice
skills.summary: Lay a strip of glaze 6 m ahead and slide the length of it. The glaze stays 5 s: you move 30% faster on it, and enemies standing on it keep slipping, losing poise every half second.
skills.verb_fit: Glaze is 'glazed ice: fast and slippery'. You are the fast, they are the slippery: the strip carries you and takes their footing.

new_mechanics.name: glaze
new_mechanics.definition: A glazed strip: the caster moves trail.caster_speed_mult faster on it; an enemy on it loses trail.payload.poise every tick_s (it keeps slipping). Fire on it clears it.

good_modifiers.word: The glaze stays 7.5 s.
Off the slide and acting sooner: recovery a quarter shorter.
A faster slide.
Whoever slips on it goes Brittle: a strike Shatters them.

bad_modifiers.why: Frost is Glaze's opposite and pulls harder (2.9 vs 2.0, polar): Glaze keeps only half its speed bonus, and the strip grips (Chill) instead of making them slip. Grip and slide cancel.
A dash that stops at bodies has nothing to pierce. Falls back.
A slide has no single target and does no damage; the op has nowhere to land but a cost cut.

skills.name: Whiteout
skills.summary: Point, 10 m: snow falls over a circle 3.5 m across for 6 s. Enemies inside cannot see past 2 m (Blinded) and gain a Chill every second. Archers inside lose you.
skills.verb_fit: Snow is 'a fall of snow that blinds and buries'. It blinds (Blinded) and it buries (Chill builds the longer they stand in it).

good_modifiers.word: A long fall: 9 s of snow.
Lands farther and covers more.
Buried and brittle: everyone in the snow can be Shattered by a strike.

bad_modifiers.why: Snow has no edge to sharpen and no blow to make heavier: no damage, no poise. Falls back.
Melt is Snow's opposite and pulls harder: melted snow is slush, not a blind, and its damage bonus has no damage to add to.
Not a shot. Falls back.

skills.name: Runoff
skills.summary: An instant line 8 m long melts the cold out of everything on it: 25 damage plus 30 for every Chill it carried, and the Chill is gone. A Frozen one counts as 5 and is freed. All of them are left Soaked.
skills.verb_fit: Melt is 'turn ice and snow to water'. Runoff turns the cold in a body to water all at once: the Chill becomes damage, and the water stays as Soaked.

new_mechanics.name: beam consume
new_mechanics.definition: A beam may 'consume_status': each enemy it hits loses that status and takes per_stack_damage per stack (a Frozen enemy counts as frozen_counts_as stacks and is freed), as a detonate does.

good_modifiers.word: A longer runoff: 11 m, a little weaker.
A narrow, hard line: 30% more damage, shorter.
Breaks the frozen ones as it melts them: +50% against Frozen, and more poise.

bad_modifiers.why: A beam is not a shot, and it already passes through everything. Falls back.
Nothing of an instant line stays. Falls back.
Cold-hardening the thing that melts: no duration to lengthen, nothing to slow. Falls back.

skills.name: Icicle
skills.summary: A spike of ice grown in your hand and thrown, slow and heavy: 80 damage, 45 poise and a Chill. It is a hard hit, so it Shatters anything Brittle or Frozen it reaches.
skills.verb_fit: Rime is 'build ice: walls, armour, spikes'. The quarter-second wind-up is the spike being built; then it is thrown. Ice's other ranged skill (Hoarline) spreads cold; this is the one that breaks it, from range.

good_modifiers.word: Grow a longer spike: 30% harder for a longer wind-up.
Leaves what it hits Brittle, so the next Icicle (or a strike) Shatters it.
A spike that goes in and through: it passes the first body and carries on.
A longer throw, a little lighter.

bad_modifiers.why: A thrown spike has no duration. Falls back.
Acts on the caster; the spike leaves you. No duration to grant; falls back.
A melted icicle is a splash of water. The maths would let it through (a damage bonus on Chilled, Soaked), but it is no longer a spike.

skills.name: Fracture
skills.summary: One enemy in reach: a hammer blow, 2.0x strike damage and 60 poise. If it is Frozen or Brittle it Shatters for +120 more, and the shards fly 4 m instead of 2.5.
skills.verb_fit: Shatter is 'break ice; brittle things burst'. Any hard hit Shatters by ice's rule; Fracture is the one built to, and pays most for it.

good_modifiers.word: Up close and harder: +20% damage, a little less reach.
What it does not break, it leaves Brittle: the bare strike after it Shatters.
A cold hammer: 2 Chill on whatever it fails to break.
Brings it down: 30% more poise damage.

bad_modifiers.why: Rime is Shatter's opposite and pulls harder (2.62 vs 1.87, polar): the hammer grows spikes but its shatter bonus is halved. Building ice on the thing that breaks it.
Not a shot. Falls back.
A blow has no duration. Falls back.

skills.name: Craze
skills.summary: Point, 9 m: fine cracks race through a 3 m circle for half a second, then everything in it is Brittle for 5 s: its next hard hit Shatters it, frozen or not. The way to break what will not freeze.
skills.verb_fit: Brittle is 'make a thing fragile'. Craze makes them fragile without freezing them, which is how ice breaks elites and heavy enemies that never lock.

good_modifiers.word: Craze a spot farther off, and a wider one.
The cracks run faster: the half-second mark drops by a quarter.
Cracks and cold together: 2 Chill as well.

bad_modifiers.why: Toughen is Brittle's opposite and pulls harder: hardening what you make fragile. No duration or speed field here; falls back.
Craze does no damage and no poise; there is nothing for the spikes to add. Falls back.
Not a shot. Falls back.

skills.name: Ice Shell
skills.summary: A shell of ice closes over you for 8 s and takes the next 80 damage. When it breaks it bursts: 40 damage and 2 Chill to everything within 2.5 m.
skills.verb_fit: Toughen is 'cold-harden it'. You harden your own skin with cold, and like all ice, when it is broken it bursts.

new_mechanics.name: absorb shell
new_mechanics.definition: self_buff 'absorb': takes that much damage before health does (after armour); when it is used up, 'on_break' bursts around you; if the time runs out first it melts with no burst.

good_modifiers.word: A shell that holds 12 s.
Worn closer, lasts 30% longer.
Carried on clean essence: 15% cheaper.

bad_modifiers.why: Brittle is Toughen's opposite: a brittle shell is no shell. The buff has no hit to carry the status; falls back.
A shell is worn, not thrown: no range or area. Falls back.
Nothing it shoots. Falls back.
